title: Composite and Decorator
idea: Composite lets you treat one object and a group of objects through the same method. Decorator wraps an object to add behaviour without editing its class.

analogy.text: Composite is a parcel that holds items or smaller parcels; weigh any of them the same way. Decorator is gift wrap: layers added outside, same box inside.
analogy.breaks: Gift wrap does nothing; each decorator layer runs its own code on every call.

points: Composite: a leaf and a group expose the same method, such as `total()`.
A group answers by asking each child, which may be another group.
Decorator: a wrapper has the same methods as the object it holds.
Each wrapper adds its step, then forwards the call to the inner object.

steps.caption: The caller holds one object and calls `find('u1')`. It cannot tell how many wrappers there are.
The outer wrapper, `LoggedRepo`, logs the call and forwards it inward.
`CachedRepo` finds no entry for `u1`, so it forwards the call too.
The real `UserRepo` does the expensive read and returns the user.
On the way back, `CachedRepo` stores the result before returning it.
Second call: `LoggedRepo` logs again, because it always runs first.
This time `CachedRepo` has the entry. It returns at once; `UserRepo` is never reached.
The caller gets the same user. Behaviour was added by stacking objects, not by editing `UserRepo`.

code.title: Composite: nested bundles
code.caption: An `Item` and a `Bundle` both answer `total()`. Add a bundle inside `combo` and run it again.

walk.text: The leaf: an `Item` returns its own price.
The composite: a `Bundle` keeps a private list of parts, leaves or bundles.
It answers `total()` by asking every child; recursion handles any depth.
`combo` holds an item and a whole bundle.
The loop never checks what kind of node it has.

code.title: Decorator: cache and log
code.caption: The code from the animation. Swap the order of the two wrappers on line 17 and compare the output.

walk.text: The real object. It knows nothing about caching or logging.
`CachedRepo` holds an inner object with the same `find` method.
On a miss it forwards the call and stores the answer.
`LoggedRepo` adds one line of output, then forwards.
Wrappers stack at the edge of the program. Order decides who runs first.
The second call is logged but served from the cache.

pitfalls: Give leaves and groups the same method names, or callers start checking `instanceof`.
Forward every method a decorator wraps; a forgotten one silently loses behaviour.
Check wrapper order: logging outside a cache logs hits; logging inside does not.

quiz.why: `Bang` asks `Loud`, which asks `Text` for `hi` and upper-cases it. `Bang` then appends `!` to `HI`.

takeaway: Composite treats parts and wholes alike; Decorator stacks behaviour around one interface.
